description.p: ArcBrush is a desktop image editor built around a node graph instead of a layer stack. You wire generators, filters, masks, warps, color tools, and exporters into a non-destructive pipeline; the graph re-runs whenever an input or parameter changes, so every step stays tunable down to the original source.
Because the pipeline is data, a single graph can produce many outputs in one run — every color variant, every export size, every file format — from the same project.

ul.li: GPU-accelerated image processing via OpenCV with OpenCL offload where available
Per-pixel operations parallelized across all CPU cores
Optional AI nodes (text-to-image, image edit, background removal, upscale); the editor itself works offline with no account
Cross-platform project files (.arcb) shared across Windows, macOS, and Linux

screenshot.caption: One graph, many outputs: palette-remapped variants exported as a batch
Wire generators, filters, and masks into a non-destructive pipeline with a live preview
Batch-process an entire folder of images and pack the results into a sprite sheet
Optional AI nodes feed generated images straight into the graph

ul.li: Pixel Sort node: reorder pixels along rows, columns, an arbitrary angle, or radial spokes and rings for glitch and drip looks
Shape node: an on-canvas manipulator to move, scale, and rotate the shape directly in the preview
Subtle UI motion across the app, with a Settings toggle to turn it all off
Smarter export conflict handling: add a numbered suffix, overwrite, or skip files already on disk
Notifications now stack, are color-coded by severity, and merge rapid duplicates
Many fixes, including color-accurate eyedropper picks on non-sRGB monitors, clipboard paste under KDE Plasma Wayland, and correct multi-GPU memory readouts
Dockable panels: rearrange the layout, pop panels out into their own windows, and save custom workspaces
Batch processing: evaluate an entire folder of images through chains of filters, color corrections, and exports in one pass
New nodes: Layer, Film Grain, Halftone, and Reroute
Node graph quality of life: alignment-guide snapping, drop-a-node-onto-a-wire splicing, and shake-to-disconnect
Expanded AI options: GPT Image 2 tiers, FLUX.2 output-size control, and new background-removal engines
